title: Probe a user buffer
description:
A kernel component receives a pointer and a length from user mode. Write `probe(address, length, alignment)`, which applies the kernel's rules:

- A zero length is always accepted (nothing will be touched).
- `alignment` (1, 2, 4 or 8) must divide `address`: otherwise `"misaligned"`.
- The whole range `address` to `address + length - 1` must lie in user space, that is below `kUserLimit` (`0x00007FFFFFFF0000`), and the addition must not wrap round: otherwise `"out of range"`.
- Otherwise `"ok"`.

Check alignment before the range.

```
probe(0x1000, 16, 8)               -> "ok"
probe(0x1004, 16, 8)               -> "misaligned"
probe(0x00007FFFFFFEFFF0, 32, 1)   -> "out of range"   (runs past the user limit)
probe(0xFFFFF80000000000, 8, 8)    -> "out of range"   (kernel address)
```
hints: Compute the last byte's address, `address + length - 1`. If it is smaller than `address`, the addition wrapped round.
The range is in user space only if its last byte is below the limit.
